definitions: A variable created in principal component analysis (PCA) that is a linear combination of the original variables and captures a certain amount of variance in the data.
One of a set of orthogonal vectors that represent the directions of maximum variance in a dataset, used to reduce dimensionality.
examples: The first Principal Component explained 60% of the variance.
We extracted three Principal Components from the dataset.
Each Principal Component is uncorrelated with the others.
